introduction: SD Law Help sends one online legal-help application to the appropriate organization. You do not need to choose between East River, Dakota Plains and Access to Justice yourself.
description: SD Law Help sends one online legal-help application to the appropriate organization. You do not need to choose between East River, Dakota Plains and Access to Justice yourself

sections.who: Providers screen finances and the civil legal issue. Some services also address older adults, veterans or domestic-violence survivors under applicable rules.
sections.get: Available assistance can range from advice and self-help support to representation. Representation is limited and requires a provider’s acceptance.
sections.docs:

  • Names of other parties.
  • Notices, court papers and dates.
sections.apply:
1. Use the common application

    Follow SD Law Help’s application link.

  2. Explain the issue and location

    Identify the county or Tribal court context and any approaching deadline.

  3. Watch for follow-up

    Check email, spam and voicemail and supply requested information.
sections.after: Clarify whether the provider is giving advice or representing you. Follow court instructions while intake is pending.
sections.sources: Checked October 1, 2026 using SD Law Help screening and routing. USA Assistance background guide. Program staff determine eligibility and available assistance.

faqs: Must I choose the right legal-aid organization?
No. The common application is routed based on your answers.
Is every accepted person represented in court?
No. The provider describes advice and self-help as well as limited representation.
Does the service handle criminal cases?
The site lists criminal law among cases it does not accept.

provenance.scope: Published eligibility, service purpose and application pathway; no unverified financial limits or deadlines included.
